areas.title: Perovskite Solar Cells
description: Research on perovskite solar cells includes the design and evaluation of small-molecule hole-transporting materials. A range of conjugated small-molecule structures has been used to examine how molecular design and fluorination affect energy-level alignment, hole mobility, film formation, interfacial charge extraction, and device stability. Scalable implementations include a dopant-free material deposited by thermally assisted blade coating and fluorinated materials used with bar-coated perovskite films.

Film formation and interface engineering have been studied through crystallization control, additive-assisted processing, moderate-temperature liquid-medium annealing with FABr passivation, and chemical-bath-deposited SnO₂ on mesoporous TiO₂. Work on large-area devices also includes an interlaboratory round-robin comparison of current density–voltage and external quantum efficiency measurements. Reliability studies using PVDF-HFP have examined performance under vacuum, illumination, heat, and gamma irradiation, including combined vacuum–light and vacuum–heat conditions. Separate reviews assessed proton irradiation in single-junction cells and failure pathways in two-terminal tandems under space-relevant stressors.

areas.title: Redox Flow Batteries
description: Graphite-felt electrodes for vanadium redox flow batteries were modified with nanostructured graphitic carbon nitride produced by thermal polymerization. Optimized surface decoration improved wettability and electrolyte access, reduced charge-transfer resistance and polarization, and supported higher energy efficiency. The modified electrode retained stable performance with negligible degradation over 1000 cycles.
A review examined MOF- and COF-containing separators and membranes for redox flow batteries, with emphasis on pore structure, ion selectivity, processability, and scale-up challenges.

areas.title: Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
description: Research on dye-sensitized solar cells has examined ZnO and TiO₂ photoanodes as frameworks for electron transport and electrolyte diffusion. Studies of branched and tetrapod-like ZnO related electrode morphology to electron and ion transport, while TiO₂ work addressed porous electrodes and gel-polymer electrolytes. PEDOT-based counter electrodes were evaluated as alternatives to platinum.

Flexible-cell research addressed low-temperature photoanode deposition, TiO₂ interfacial layers on titanium substrates, sealing, and stability under prolonged illumination and heat. Mesoporous SiO₂ was also examined in bifacial and back-illuminated devices. Large-area module studies evaluated photoanode treatment, dye-sensitization conditions, electrolyte injection, module design, and polymer sealing in modules up to 10 × 15 cm.
